newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan bank chief arrested on corruption charges.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan bank chief arrested on corruption charges.

text.p: Pakistani investigators arrested Shaukat Ali Kazmi, president of the privatised Allied Bank Ltd (ABL), at his home in Lahore, officials said on Sunday.

"Kazmi was arrested on Saturday on several charges of mismanagement, violation of regulations on lending and corruption," an official of the Federal Investigation Agency in Karachi said. He gave no details.
Lawyers for Kazmi could not be reached for comment.
Kazmi was the first executive of a private bank to be arrested since Pakistan's caretaker government launched a campaign to weed out corruption from the financial sector.

Newspapers said Kazmi was close to some associates of former prime minister Benazir Bhutto, whose government was dismissed by President Farooq Leghari on November 5 on disputed charges of corruption and misrule.
Last month M.B. Abbasi, former head of the state-run National Bank of Pakistan, was arrested on similar charges.
Kazmi became president of ABL after his predecessor, Khalid Latif was arrested in January 1995, on corruption charges.
Latif is in jail, awaiting trial.

ABL was privatised in September 1991 when the government of former prime minister Nawaz Sharif sold 26 percent of its shares to employees who had formed an Allied Management Group. The group raised its stake to 51 percent in August 1993.
The bank has an authorised capital of 500 million rupees ($12.43 million) and paid-up capital of 272 million rupees.
